title: Human methylarginine sites, context marks, cancer and germline variants and their mutation propensity, v1.7.0 (PTM_Pipeline)
description: The human protein arginine methylation sites of DeAngelo, Silverstein & Shechter, Cell Chem Biol 33:1404-1421 (2026), with the code that builds them and the Methylarginine Site Explorer website, and tables of other human protein modifications beside them. v1.7.0 adds the mutation propensity of every candidate residue in each source (TCGA, DepMap, ClinVar, gnomAD): observed against expected changes under codon mutability, within each protein, with a binomial test and Benjamini-Hochberg q at every known site and every changed residue, TCGA and DepMap with their own spectra and with and without hypermutated samples (above 10 coding calls per Mb), gnomAD and ClinVar with gnomAD's methylation-aware germline rates (the mutation_rate_methylation_bins table of the gnomAD v2.1.1 flagship paper; ClinVar descriptive); site-set tests; frequencies per TCGA project and DepMap lineage; each sample's mutation burden; and positive controls (recurrent cancer hotspots and the oncohistone residues of H3). v1.6.0 adds the somatic missense and stop changes at every candidate residue of the site sets (every arginine, lysine, serine, threonine and tyrosine of the reviewed canonical proteins, a known site or not) in TCGA tumors (the MC3 calls of the PanCancer Atlas, 10,294 tumor samples; GDC open access) and DepMap 24Q4 cell lines (CC BY 4.0), with the site sets each residue belongs to and per-protein background counts: 274,408 arginine, 61,510 lysine, 142,576 serine, 59,012 threonine and 25,757 tyrosine changes in tumors. It also adds the germline variants there: ClinVar (classifications, review stars, conditions; NCBI places no restrictions on its use) and gnomAD v4.1 exomes (allele counts and frequencies; CC0), 829,234 ClinVar variants and 3,602,080 gnomAD variants at those residues. v1.5.1 adds, for the methyllysine, lysine (acetylation and other acylations, ubiquitination, SUMOylation) and phosphorylation sites of v1.5.0, the site-level interaction tables the methylarginine release has: PDB interfaces with each entry's method, paper and the state of the residue it models, RNA and DNA contacts in structures with the bound sequences, and RNA-binding evidence from cells (5,178 methyllysine, 90,876 lysine and 142,415 phosphorylation sites). v1.5.0 keeps the methylarginine data of v1.4.3 unchanged (its files are carried over byte for byte) and adds tables of context marks, for sites of other marks to read: human lysine methylation, phosphorylation, lysine acylation (14 acyl types, acetylation also on its own), ubiquitination and SUMOylation sites, merged from UniProt (release 2026_04, CC BY 4.0), iPTMnet (release 6.2, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with its own score), Berryhill et al. (Sci Rep 13:377, 2023; lysine methylation; article CC BY 4.0, supplements without a notice), Ochoa et al. (Nat Biotechnol 38:365, 2020; phosphorylation sites and functional scores; article not open access), Hendriks et al. (Nat Struct Mol Biol 24:325, 2017; SUMO-2) and Akimov et al. (Nat Struct Mol Biol 25:631, 2018; ubiquitination), one row per residue and state with the sources, the evidence class and the PubMed IDs, and the arginine methylation records of UniProt and iPTMnet as a cross-check; CPLM 4.0 is not a source (it states no license); the release stays CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. v1.4.3 keeps every site and value of v1.4.2 and says where each interaction record at a site comes from: its PDB entry, IntAct interaction, crosslinking study or predicted model, method, species and paper, the state of the site in that experiment, and what the record shows (the partner methylates the site, binds it methylated, binds it unmodified, binds a region holding it, and more), with flags for records to check; PDB entries that model a site methylated are read in full, including peptides PDBe-KB does not map to the human protein. v1.4.2 has 11,632 sites on 4,439 proteins, and 2,396 lower-confidence sites, as v1.4.1, and adds a layer of annotation, maps of the cell: where the methylated proteins sit by four maps beside the Human Protein Atlas (the Human Cell Map, organelle IP, chromatin probability, and the nuclear speckle, lamina and PML-body proteomes), each tested against the proteins it places and within PaxDb abundance deciles, compartment by compartment and in three regions (the nucleus, the cytoplasm outside the organelles, and the organelles and membranes), and where the RNAs bound by proteins with eCLIP data gather (APEX-seq, nuclear-body APEX2-seq, TSA-seq and Hi-C subcompartments); on the website, selections open on the Overview, where every section is retested on them. It also corrects the continuity correction of the Mantel-Haenszel test (190 p-values change, none across q <= 0.05). v1.4.1 keeps every site and value of v1.4.0 and repeats each protein-level over-representation test within PaxDb protein abundance deciles (Mantel-Haenszel), beside the test it repeats. v1.4.0 kept every site of v1.3.1 and added 31 from Lu et al. 2024 (HeLa). Five layers of annotation sit beside the sites without adding, removing or moving any: PRMT knockouts, knockdowns and inhibitors from five studies, each site called at twofold and q < 0.05 and by the published criteria; cancer genetics (DepMap 24Q4 and PRISM 24Q2 dependencies of the methylated proteins, and the changes at each methylarginine in TCGA tumors and DepMap cell lines); Reactome 97 pathways; PaxDb 6.1 protein abundance; and experiments on the methylation of a site or protein, curated from the literature. releases/v1.7.0/README.md says what v1.7.0 adds, releases/v1.6.0/README.md what v1.6.0 adds, releases/v1.5.1/README.md what v1.5.1 adds, and releases/v1.5.0/CHANGES.md what v1.5.0 changed since v1.4.3; the earlier versions (v1.6.0, v1.5.1, v1.5.0, v1.4.3, v1.4.2, v1.4.1, v1.4.0, v1.3.1, v1.3.0, v1.2.0, v1.1.0 and the published v1.0.0) are also included.
